impact_groups.state_owner: WorkerGate retains native generations/handles, immutable outcomes, quarantine and same-home delivery; callback registry retains exact per-processor scopes and action handles.
impact_groups.origin: Adaptation of upstream curated synchronization and manager startup. WorkerGate/callback scopes/process-final aggregation/delivery are project additions, not moved upstream declarations.
invariants: Preserve plugin/auth/marketplace policy gating and Git→HTTP→bootstrap-only-export ordering.
Stopped or uncertain cleanup must not become an ordinary retry/fallback error.
Reserve callback ownership before spawn; close registration before process-wide native stop.
Join exact handles; observer cancellation retains custody; immutable operation outcome is distinct from cleanup completion.
Same lexical absolute home may subscribe/replay once per scope; other homes remain UnsupportedHome.
Activation rename and SHA publication are still separate filesystem steps; no transactional durability claim.
hazards: New upstream background callbacks can escape existing scope coverage.
Changing home identity, success latch or generation attachment ordering can deliver stale A work to replacement B.
MCP descendants are not covered merely because their calling callback returned.

impact_groups.state_owner: Executable-created ProcessFinalCapability starts a process singleton holding an independent native watchdog until runtime/native-main teardown is observed.
impact_groups.origin: Project-authored support. It is neither a separately installed subsystem nor proof the final minimal kernel is achieved.
invariants: First process-final call fixes absolute200s graceful and205s forced-initiation deadlines; later calls cannot renew them.
Embedded lifecycle uses optional authority and must not arm or irreversibly close the process clock.
Exit124 timeout,125 watchdog unavailable and126 explicit force retain cleanup/durability uncertainty.
Disarm only after actual native-main join and runtime destruction.
hazards: std::process::exit can be delayed by exit handlers;205s is not an absolute OS termination guarantee.
Moving finalization into the async main future can hide blocking runtime teardown.

impact_groups.state_owner: arg0 owns native main invocation, Tokio runtime teardown and dispatch/tempdir lifetime.
invariants: Finish watchdog after native thread join on success and panic paths.
Preserve existing sandbox alias dispatch and dispatch paths.
hazards: Upstream runtime ownership/refactoring can move the actual teardown boundary without a textual conflict.

impact_groups.state_owner: CLI/standalone binaries supply process-final capability; ordinary exec/TUI library entrypoints remain embedded.
impact_groups.origin: Adapted upstream CLI/exec/TUI dispatch plus project-authored cleanup helpers.
invariants: Fence process admission at final-exit onset before local drains.
Propagate capability across actual exec/review/App Server/TUI dispatch.
Preserve original operation error if cleanup also fails.
TUI LocalStateDbStartupError remains recoverable and must permit in-process repair/retry.
hazards: New upstream early returns or altered error wrapping can bypass cleanup or poison a recoverable second invocation.
Do not infer native tool-execution or TUI extraction from these support changes.

impact_groups.state_owner: Processor owns callback scope; selected storage/search guards outlive abortable request tasks; app-server coordinates owner shutdown.
impact_groups.origin: Adapted upstream service processing and in-process client; project-authored guards and process-final helpers.
invariants: process_final defaults None independently of signal-handler installation.
During final shutdown use remaining absolute grace; embedded budgets remain distinct.
Close admission before drain; observe exact aborted handles.
Keep storage/search drains parallel and preserve accepted-write uncertainty on failures.
hazards: Timeout receipt is not a completed join or durability receipt.
Parallelizing new service cleanup may still require explicit dependency order.
Global MCP custody and publication recovery remain open.

impact_groups.state_owner: App Server client retains coordinator/worker custody on owning runtime; stdio bridges native input/signal paths to executable authority.
impact_groups.origin: Upstream already supplied dedicated stdio threads and a local45s watchdog. Current adaptation replaces watchdog authority and adds EOF-triggered arming. Separate client shutdown owner is project-added.
invariants: Dropped shutdown observer must not discard the coordinator or actual worker.
Stdio SIGTERM/native stdin completion/forwarded EOF must reach the shared clock without requiring responsive Tokio logging.
Clamp205s facade budget to active global grace; do not renew it.
hazards: Native stdin/stdout threads can block until process exit; no all-native-threads-joined claim.
Merging upstream watchdog changes must retain installed storage cleanup budget and explicit uncertainty.

Repeated gateway close calls share a deadline and retain prior failure.
Do not close buffered stdout while its reader is live; nonzero/forced/lingering-reader outcomes preserve unknown accepted writes.
hazards: Synchronous stdlib shutdown/server_close work is not preemptible by constants alone.
Current-source real Launch/slow-storage acceptance remains required; static clock comparison is not runtime proof.
